advances:
At the fixed normalization \(q=1\), \(x_i=5/21\), the universal
mixed-area and incidence-slack bounds prove the accepted midpoint-ledger
target exactly on one explicit scalar region.  The accepted scalar
constraints force every possible counterexample strictly outside that
region.  They reduce the remaining scalar outer region to three short
inequality groups and give the exact mixed-area/cap-shape or \(\Xi\)
correction still needed there.  This is a scalar split and missing-shape
calibration, not a proof of the full midpoint-ledger inequality.
author: /root/mp_r54_ledger_scalar_split
proof:
At (1), accepted fact `0009896ebff12f31` computes
\[
\eta>\frac67.
\tag{20}
\]
Also
\[
\eta=w+3d_R+6r_{123}>w
\tag{21}
\]
because \(d_R\geq0\) and \(r_{123}>0\).  Accepted fact
`af9178be3aa6202a` gives \(\eta\geq c_*\).  The effective lower bound in
accepted fact `9b267b01d2864206` is retained as well, but it is weaker
than (20): its definition gives
\[
c_{\rm eff}\leq\frac{7L}{16}<\frac67,
\]
since \(L<1\).  We derive a sharper exact upper bound on \(D\) below.

We first use crossings and tails.  Write
\[
u_i=\sum_{J\ni i}p_J,\qquad
v_i=m-x_i.
\]
The \(i\)-th crossing and left tail give
\[
h=u_i+v_i+c_i\leq c_i+m,
\]
so
\[
u_i\leq m-v_i=x_i=\frac5{21}.
\]
Consequently
\[
s_P+2d_P=\sum_i u_i\leq\frac57.
\]
Since
\[
w=s_P+4d_P\leq2(s_P+2d_P),
\]
this proves \(0\leq w\leq10/7\), and proves all of (7).

Accepted fact `084bf2f472bf29c7` gives the exact \(W=0\) identity
\[
2p=\frac{69}{7}+k+\eta,
\qquad
k=2p-\frac{69}{7}-\eta.
\tag{22}
\]
Moreover
\[
M=p+s_P+d_P
\geq
p+\frac{s_P+4d_P}{4}
=p+\frac w4.
\tag{23}
\]
The outer-centroid argument in accepted fact `b8e22f6a4b26ea94`
shows that every table still in the canonical counterexample branch
must satisfy
\[
M\leq m+k.
\tag{24}
\]
Otherwise \(M>m+k\), and the centroid of \(A_0\) already has depth
strictly larger than the target.  Combining (22)-(24) gives
\[
p+\frac w4
\leq
\frac{12}{7}+2p-\frac{69}{7}-\eta,
\]
or equivalently
\[
p\geq\frac{57}{7}+\eta+\frac w4.
\tag{25}
\]
Together with (20), this gives \(p>9+w/4\geq9\), proving the first
part of (11).

We now retain the total deficit and feed it back into the accepted scale
bridge.  Put
\[
\Delta_0=4k-
\left(\sqrt M+\sqrt{\frac{12}{7}}\right)^2.
\]
Equation (24) gives \(k\geq M-m\), and hence
\[
\Delta_0
\geq
3M-5m-2\sqrt{Mm}.
\tag{26}
\]
By (23), (25), and (20),
\[
\frac{M}{m}
\geq
\frac{p+w/4}{12/7}
>
\frac{9}{12/7}
=\frac{21}{4}.
\]
The function \(3t-5-2\sqrt t\) is strictly increasing for
\(t>1/9\).  Dividing (26) by \(m=12/7\) therefore gives the exact strict
bound
\[
\Delta_0
>
\frac{12}{7}\left(\frac{43}{4}-\sqrt{21}\right)
=
\frac{129-12\sqrt{21}}{7}.
\tag{27}
\]

The strengthened bridge in accepted fact `b8e22f6a4b26ea94`, with
\(q=1\), is
\[
\frac1D
\geq
\left(
2\sqrt{r_{123}}
+
\frac{
\sqrt{12/7}
+
\sqrt{2028/7+28\eta+7\Delta_0}
}{7}
\right)^2.
\tag{28}
\]
By (20) and (27), the second radicand in (28) is strictly larger than
\[
\frac{2028}{7}+24+129-12\sqrt{21}
=
\frac{3099}{7}-12\sqrt{21}
=
\left(21-\sqrt{\frac{12}{7}}\right)^2.
\tag{29}
\]
The last square root is positive.  Dropping only the positive
\(2\sqrt{r_{123}}\) term in (28), and using (29), gives
\[
\frac1D
>
\left(
\frac{\sqrt{12/7}+21-\sqrt{12/7}}7
\right)^2
=9.
\]
Thus \(0<D<1/9\), completing (9).

The function in (2) has derivative
\[
\Lambda'(p)
=
-\frac{39}{4}
+\frac94\sqrt{\frac5{21p}},
\]
which is negative for \(p\geq9\).  At \(p=9\),
\[
\Lambda(9)
=
-\frac{309}{14}
+\frac92\sqrt{\frac{15}{7}}
<0.
\tag{30}
\]
Indeed, the last inequality is equivalent to
\[
21\sqrt{\frac{15}{7}}<103,
\]
and squaring the positive sides gives \(945<10609\).
Monotonicity, \(p>9\), \(w\geq0\), and (30) prove the second part of
(11) and the sharpened uniform bound (12).

For comparison with the fixed-ratio determinant terms displayed in
accepted fact `0009896ebff12f31`, here
\[
A_k=\frac{36}{5},\qquad c_k=\frac{10}{21},
\]
and exact substitution gives
\[
d_{1k}=\frac{496125}{4190209}>\frac19.
\]
The last comparison is the integer inequality
\(9\cdot496125=4465125>4190209\).
However
\[
\frac{\sqrt{A_k}-c_k}{1+c_k}>1,
\]
because \(\sqrt{36/5}>41/21\).  Hence \(d_{2k}=0\), so the accepted
minimum \(\delta\) is still zero.  Thus \(D<1/9\) does not by itself
close the high-clip scalar survivor; a new cap-shape input is still
necessary.

It remains to derive the exact ledger split.  The universal planar
mixed-area inequality specified in the subgoal gives
\[
\mathcal V_i\geq
\sqrt{|P||C_i|}
=
\sqrt{\frac{5p}{21}}.
\]
This proves (3).  Substituting
\[
\sum_i\mathcal V_i
=
3\sqrt{\frac{5p}{21}}+\kappa
\]
into (4), and moving the universal term to the right, proves the exact
equivalence (5), because
\[
\frac{39p}{4}+w-\frac{1839}{28}
-
\frac92\sqrt{\frac{5p}{21}}
=w-\Lambda(p).
\]
The conclusion (6), and its maximality relative to only
\(\kappa,\Xi\geq0\), follow immediately.

Accepted fact `6e4bb19f9157027f` also gives the exact identity
\[
7\eta
=
\frac{39p}{4}+w-\frac{1671}{28}
-\frac32\sum_i\mathcal V_i-3\Xi.
\tag{31}
\]
Substitute (3) into (31) and rearrange.  The result is (13).
Nonnegativity of its left side gives
\[
7\eta\leq w-\Lambda(p)+6,
\]
which is (8).  At the scalar level, this is the fixed-ratio form of the
overlap-corrected multiplicity inequality in accepted fact
`2bb72698f0248a65`; the identity (31) records its two geometric slacks
separately.  Combining (8) with (20)-(21) proves (10).  Comparing (5)
and (13) proves (14), so no scalar inference has been mislabeled as the
missing shape theorem.

For completeness, we prove the cap-shape lower bound (16).  For planar
convex polytopes, the area polynomial
\[
|aK+bL|
=
a^2|K|+2ab\,\mathcal V(K,L)+b^2|L|
\qquad(a,b\geq0)
\]
shows that mixed area is additive in either Minkowski argument.  One
may verify this directly by merging the counterclockwise edge-vector
lists and expanding the shoelace determinant.  Therefore
\[
\sum_i\mathcal V(P,C_i)
=
\mathcal V(P,C_1+C_2+C_3).
\tag{32}
\]
Planar Brunn--Minkowski, first for the three caps and then for \(P\) and
their sum, gives
\[
\sqrt{|C_1+C_2+C_3|}
\geq
\sum_i\sqrt{|C_i|}
=3\sqrt{\frac5{21}},
\]
\[
\mathcal V(P,C_1+C_2+C_3)
\geq
\sqrt{p\,|C_1+C_2+C_3|}.
\]
Using (15) in (32) proves
\[
\sum_i\mathcal V_i
\geq
3\sqrt{\frac{5p}{21}}+\sqrt p\,\omega_C,
\]
which is (16).  Substituting this lower bound into the left side of
(5) proves (19); (17) and (18) are its two one-term specializations.
The remaining conditional rows of accepted fact
`2186f01c16b1f4e3` may shrink the necessary outer survivor (7)-(9), but
are not used as a substitute for the unproved lower bounds
(17)-(19).  This completes the exact scalar elimination without
claiming the full shape inequality.
statement:
Assume the complete canonical finite-interior common-plane hypotheses,
exact-cell convention, \(M\geq m\), crossings, canonical tails, \(W=0\),
all-double positive \(Q\)-support, and
\(r_1r_2r_3r_{123}>0\).  Normalize
\[
q=q_{123}=1,\qquad
x_1=x_2=x_3=\frac5{21},\qquad
m=\frac{12}{7}.
\tag{1}
\]
Use the notation of accepted fact `6e4bb19f9157027f`:
\[
p=p_\varnothing,\qquad
w=w_P=s_P+4d_P,\qquad
\eta=w+3d_R+6r_{123},
\]
\[
\Xi\geq0,\qquad
\mathcal V_i=\mathcal V(P,C_i),\qquad |C_i|=\frac5{21}.
\]
Define
\[
\Lambda(p)
=
\frac{1839}{28}-\frac{39p}{4}
+\frac92\sqrt{\frac{5p}{21}},
\tag{2}
\]
and the mixed-area correction
\[
\kappa
=
\sum_{i=1}^3\mathcal V_i
-3\sqrt{\frac{5p}{21}}
\geq0.
\tag{3}
\]

The midpoint-ledger target of accepted fact `6e4bb19f9157027f`,
\[
\frac32\sum_{i=1}^3\mathcal V_i+3\Xi
\geq
\frac{39p}{4}+w-\frac{1839}{28},
\tag{4}
\]
is equivalent to
\[
\boxed{\quad
\frac32\kappa+3\Xi\geq w-\Lambda(p).
\quad}
\tag{5}
\]
Consequently the baseline bounds \(\kappa\geq0\), \(\Xi\geq0\) prove
(4) throughout
\[
w\leq\Lambda(p).
\tag{6}
\]
This is the largest region that these two nonnegativity bounds alone can
certify: when \(w>\Lambda(p)\), their formal extremal values
\(\kappa=\Xi=0\) do not imply (5).

Let \(c_*>0\) be the constant of accepted fact
`af9178be3aa6202a`.  Every scalar table coming from a full realization
under (1) lies in the following outer survivor, where
\(D=1/|\mathcal T_Q|\):
\[
0\leq w\leq\frac{10}{7},\qquad
\eta>w,\qquad
\eta>\frac67,\qquad
\eta\geq c_*,
\tag{7}
\]
\[
7\eta\leq w-\Lambda(p)+6,
\tag{8}
\]
\[
p\geq\frac{57}{7}+\eta+\frac w4,
\qquad
0<D<\frac19.
\tag{9}
\]
Equivalently, (7)-(8) may be written as the single interval condition
\[
\max\left\{w,\frac67\right\}<\eta
\leq\frac{w-\Lambda(p)+6}{7},
\qquad
\eta\geq c_*,
\qquad
0\leq w\leq\frac{10}{7}.
\tag{10}
\]
The strict and weak lower bounds on \(\eta\) in (10) are intentionally
kept separate when \(c_*>6/7\).

In fact every point in this outer survivor satisfies
\[
p>9,
\qquad
\Lambda(p)<0.
\tag{11}
\]
Thus (6) contains no scalar point allowed by (7)-(9): all allowed points
have
\[
w-\Lambda(p)
>
\frac{309}{14}-\frac92\sqrt{\frac{15}{7}}
>0.
\tag{12}
\]
More precisely, the ledger identity in accepted fact
`6e4bb19f9157027f` gives the exact correction ledger
\[
\boxed{\quad
\frac32\kappa+3\Xi
=
w-\Lambda(p)-(7\eta-6).
\quad}
\tag{13}
\]
Hence (8) is exactly the nonnegativity consequence of (13), and the
amount required in (5) exceeds the correction recorded in (13) by
exactly
\[
7\eta-6>0.
\tag{14}
\]

There is also a cap-shape formulation.  Put
\[
\omega_C
=
\sqrt{|C_1+C_2+C_3|}
-3\sqrt{\frac5{21}}
\geq0.
\tag{15}
\]
Then
\[
\kappa\geq\sqrt p\,\omega_C.
\tag{16}
\]
Therefore either of the following pointwise lower bounds is sufficient
for (4):
\[
\boxed{\quad
\Xi\geq\frac{w-\Lambda(p)}3,
\quad}
\tag{17}
\]
or
\[
\boxed{\quad
\omega_C\geq
\frac{2\bigl(w-\Lambda(p)\bigr)}{3\sqrt p}.
\quad}
\tag{18}
\]
The exact tradeoff supplied by the same lower-bound method is
\[
\boxed{\quad
\omega_C+\frac{2\Xi}{\sqrt p}
\geq
\frac{2\bigl(w-\Lambda(p)\bigr)}{3\sqrt p}.
\quad}
\tag{19}
\]
If the actual mixed-area correction \(\kappa\), rather than the lower
bound (16), is retained, (5) is the exact necessary-and-sufficient
tradeoff.
